record.title: White blood cell count and neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio in uncomplicated and complicated canine babesiosis caused by Babesia canis canis
record.journal: University of Zagreb University Computing Centre (SRCE)
record.abstract: KučeR, N., V. MatijatKo, i. Kiš, D. GRDeN, M. BRKljačić, j.FoRšeK, Z. ŽVoRc, R. BaRić RaFaj: White blood cell count and neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio in uncomplicated and complicated canine babesiosis caused by Babesia canis canis.

screening.species: B. canis canis (confirmed per title; natural infection, Croatia)
screening.rationale: Based on the hrcak.srce.hr landing page abstract (Kučer et al., Veterinarski arhiv 78(4):321-330, 2008, in window): 60 naturally infected dogs (30 uncomplicated, 30 complicated) were sampled serially. In the complicated group, WBC, neutrophil percentage and NLR were higher and lymphocytes lower, and NLR is proposed as a severity and prognostic marker.
